prior_narrative.tldr: Agent memory research started with how to store conversational memory: AutoViewMem proposed self-configuring views instead of fixed granularities. A benchmark post then asked how to evaluate long-term memory beyond the context window.
prior_narrative.whats_new: PACMI (Oct 5) tackles stale memory: it invalidates dependent memories when an upstream fact is outdated, tracked through provenance.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Agents that persist memory across sessions need an update and invalidation policy, not only a retrieval layer; stale memories are a reliability risk that retrieval benchmarks do not catch.

status.detail: Research focus is moving from how to store memory to how to keep it correct and measure it.

storylines.latest_title: TypeSafe AI Releases Jev: A Decision-Only Model That Returns Typed Probabilities Instead of Text

prior_narrative.tldr: TypeSafe AI introduced Jev as a "System One" model that only decides, classifies, routes, and scores, claiming over 100x the speed and 200x the cost efficiency of small frontier LLMs. CEO Diogo Almeida pitched it as built for production reliability, and Simon Willison argued "decision models" is the better name.

prior_narrative.why_it_matters: A purpose-built model that's 100x faster and 200x cheaper than a small frontier LLM is a strong fit for the classify/route/score steps buried inside most agent pipelines — the exact spots teams currently overpay a general-purpose LLM to handle.

storylines.latest_title: Safety of Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems

prior_narrative.tldr: Three arXiv papers in two weeks treat multi-agent systems as a shared-state problem. MACE (Sep 18) stores collaboration traces in an adaptive memory graph; a Sep 29 paper ties task regions to agent responsibility, handoffs, and memory access.
prior_narrative.whats_new: A Sep 30 paper examines safety of latent communication, where agents exchange internal representations instead of text to cut token and latency cost.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Memory, handoffs, and inter-agent channels are where multi-agent systems break in production; these papers propose mechanisms, not production results.

status.detail: Three papers, all single-paper claims with no independent replication yet.

beats.headline: MACE reuses collaboration traces through adaptive memory graphs
beats.summary: Preserves each action's prerequisites so agents can reuse plan, verify, and repair procedures.

beats.headline: Topological coherence couples workflow, responsibility, and memory access
beats.summary: Task regions define tool scope; cross-region dependencies become handoffs.

beats.headline: Latent communication trades text overhead for a new safety surface

open_questions: Does any of these approaches ship in an open-source agent framework?
Do latent channels get an independent safety evaluation beyond the proposing paper?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Keep inter-agent messages as inspectable text in anything audited; treat latent communication as research until a safety evaluation replicates.
